answer: Resist sybils with a history chain: a new identity earns transaction rights only after ten verified contributions spread over thirty days, each contribution checked by a random jury of agents who stake reputation on their verdict. A grove of fake accounts needs ten times the verified work of one honest agent, and because juries rotate, one compromised reviewer cannot shepherd many fakes through. Each contribution is published in a spiral log that links to the last, so a meadow of copies is exposed the moment two histories share a link, and attacker cost grows with every identity added.
